task.goal: A log collector receives UTF-8 NDJSON in arbitrary byte chunks. Its parser sometimes loses records when a chunk ends in the middle of a UTF-8 character or a line. Fix the parser in stream_records.py without changing its public function. Run the visible tests, add a focused regression test if useful, and validate the fix. Do not edit benchmark metadata; only this copied project is your workspace.

result.text:
I'll start by inspecting the workspace and the parser.Both bugs are in the same line: `chunk.decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")` discards a trailing partial UTF-8 sequence permanently (the bytes are gone before the next chunk arrives). Fix with an incremental decoder so partial bytes are carried across chunks.Now a focused regression test for byte-by-byte chunking and end-of-stream truncation.My test's expectation was wrong, not the fix: a *truncated JSON line* still leaves `{"name":"` to be parsed at end-of-stream, which raises — the same as before my change. The real end-of-stream case is dangling partial *bytes* with no dangling content.**Fixed.** `stream_records.py:15` decoded each chunk in isolation with `errors="ignore"`, so bytes of a UTF-8 character split across chunks were discarded before the next chunk arrived; the corrupted line then failed to parse or lost data.

The fix swaps `chunk.decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")` for a `codecs.getincrementaldecoder("utf-8")(errors="ignore")` instance that buffers partial sequences between chunks and is flushed with `final=True` at end of stream. Line reassembly through `pending` was already correct and is untouched, as is the public `parse_records(chunks)` signature.

Added regression tests (`test_stream_records.py`) covering a 4-byte emoji plus CJK character split one byte per chunk, a mid-character split in a final line with no trailing newline, and dangling partial bytes after complete records.

`python -m unittest -v test_stream_records` → 6 tests pass (3 pre-existing, 3 new). One expectation of mine was wrong on the first run and corrected: a truncated *JSON line* still raises `json.JSONDecodeError` — pre-existing behavior, unchanged; only dangling partial bytes that complete no line are dropped.

Only `stream_records.py` and `test_stream_records.py` were modified; no benchmark metadata touched. Limitation: `errors="ignore"` means genuinely invalid bytes are silently discarded, matching prior tolerance policy.
